source.title: Proxy-Normalizing Activations to Match Batch Normalization while Removing Batch Dependence
source.authors: A. Labatie; Dominic Masters; Z. Eaton-Rosen; C. Luschi

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses batch normalization as a baseline while evaluating its own batch-independent normalization method. It does not measure training speed, learning-rate tolerance, or whether the claim versions’ training-error outcomes hold.
record.gate_note: The paper reports final validation accuracies for BN and alternative normalization methods, and training accuracies for batch-independent methods. These results compare normalization methods’ final performance, not the training-speed or training-error claims in V1–V6. The Fixup and other listed studies are cited, not tested.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates proxy normalization using final validation accuracy, ImageNet training accuracy, and activation statistics. It does not measure any version's specified training-error outcome, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, initialization comparison, or stability-threshold dynamics. BN serves as a comparator for the proposed method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they argue that LN/GN combined with proxy normalization reproduces BN's beneficial normalization properties and broadly matches its behavior and classification performance without batch dependence. They report higher ImageNet training accuracies than alternative batch-independent methods, while emphasizing regularization dependence and omitting BN training accuracies. Their broad performance conclusion should retain the documented architecture and regularization qualifications; they do not demonstrate equal training speed or learning-rate tolerance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a new proxy-normalized activation combined with GN or LN, comparing final classification performance with BN. Its experiments do not reproduce the training-speed or learning-rate measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported validation accuracy varies with normalization method, architecture, dataset, regularization, and EfficientNet variant. CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 comparisons use five ResNet sizes; ImageNet comparisons cover ResNets, ResNeXts and EfficientNets.

fits_no_version.finding: GN+PN's final validation accuracy depends on architecture and regularization. Without extra regularization it trails BN on several ImageNet architectures and all five CIFAR-100 models; with extra regularization it exceeds BN on ImageNet ResNets and four of five CIFAR-100 models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Group normalization with proxy normalization can match or exceed BN's final classification accuracy under suitable architecture and regularization choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–3 and Figures 2, 5 and 6 characterize channel collapse and instance-statistics constraints, and show that proxy normalization can reproduce BN-like activation statistics. These measures do not establish training speed or trainable depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Proxy normalization can mitigate channel-wise collapse associated with layer normalization while retaining variability in instance statistics.

record.problems: The results relevant to normalization comparisons are final validation accuracies rather than learning curves, training speed, or training error. The authors state that BN training accuracies are not comparable because of BN’s inherent regularization, and therefore report training accuracies only for batch-independent methods. Reported means and standard deviations are across 3 runs for ImageNet results and 10 runs for CIFAR results.
record.rows_left_out: Training-accuracy tables 9–11 compare batch-independent approaches and provide no BN training-accuracy baseline; they do not test any listed version, so they are not extracted as rows. Other alternative-normalization validation results in Tables 2, 4, 8, 15 and 16 are omitted because the selected rows already capture the BN versus GN+PN comparison central to the fit finding.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR-10/100 training classification error, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on size, duration and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and benefits of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with plain-network depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization and Fixup exceptions.
Effects of initialization choices on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Recovery above initial stability limits, curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to thresholds.
BN's effect on speed of accuracy gains and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's comparative speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: Tables 9–11 are already declared in rows_left_out and concern ImageNet rather than V1's CIFAR training-error outcome. Activation-collapse results and IN numerical instability do not test V4 or V5 without the specified initialization comparisons or stability-threshold measurements.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 training classification error, random initialization, corrupted or random labels, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual depth effects on training error; special initialization for plain tanh networks; Fixup training without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, training speed, and trainable depth.
Training above stability thresholds, curvature changes, loss trajectories, and divergence.
Whether BN speeds accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates, and whether Fixup trains residual networks as fast and stably without normalization.
